newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Jinro restructuring news to buoy Seoul stocks.
newsitem.headline: Jinro restructuring news to buoy Seoul stocks.

text.p: News that South Korea's 19th largest conglomerate, Jinro Group, would sell off unprofitable businesses are expected to push Seoul stocks higher on Tuesday, brokers said.
"The news report is good news in that the group's effort will improve its finanical status," said Lee Young-won, a broker at Daewoo Securities.

The composite stock index ended 7.25 points higher at 704.20 on Monday. Jinro said on Monday it would sell its canned food and soft drinks businesses as part of a plan to raise more than 1.2 trillion won by the end of 1998.
Some brokers said the Jinro effect would be short-lived as investor jitters over the group's financial problems could revive anytime.
The group said Jinro plans to boost its equity-to-asset ratio to 13 percent by the end of this year and 24.7 percent by 1998 from the current 4.43 percent.
Brokers said overall bullish sentiment was backed by rising customer deposits with securities houses and ample liquidity.
Petrochemical shares would be in demand on falling international naphtha prices.
